extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/agents) handling filing-date and application-completeness matters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining whether a U.S. patent application is entitled to a filing date and the required content/formalities (written description, claims, drawings), the notices to be mailed (Notice of Incomplete Application; Notice of Omitted Item(s)), available applicant responses (petitions, amendments, submissions), and examiner/OPAP processing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is entitled to a filing date only if it contains something that can be construed as a written description (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application does not contain anything that can be construed as a written description, OPAP will mail a Notice of Incomplete Application indicating the application lacks the specification required by 35 U.S.C. 112. Applicant may (A) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with evidence to establish prior receipt, (B) submit the omitted specification (including at least one claim) with an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63/1.64 and accept that submission date as the filing date, or (C) submit an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(a). Petitions must be accompanied by sufficient evidence (37 CFR 1.181(b)) such as a date-stamped postcard receipt (MPEP § 503). The 2-month period for response (where applicable) is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim requirement for filing date (nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) must include at least one claim to be entitled to a filing date; the omission of a claim makes the application incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a nonprovisional application does not contain at least one claim, a Notice of Incomplete Application will be mailed setting a period for submitting a claim; the filing date will be the date of receipt of at least one claim. An oath/declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 and 1.64 referring to the claim being submitted is required. A preliminary amendment that cancels all claims without presenting new or substitute claims will be disapproved; the Office will treat such an application as containing only a single claim for fee purposes. Applicant may alternatively file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(c)(2) to convert the application to a 35 U.S.C. 111(b) (provisional-style) application (must be filed within 12 months of deposit and meet other requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing requirement for filing date (35 U.S.C. 113)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must furnish a drawing where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter sought to be patented (35 U.S.C. 113, first sentence); an application is entitled to a filing date only if it contains at least one drawing figure when a drawing is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed without drawings are inspected to determine whether a drawing is referred to in the specification and whether a drawing is necessary for understanding the invention. The Office has practiced that process/method claims and many composition applications usually do not require drawings for a filing date. Specific situations where drawings are usually not necessary include: (A) coated articles/products where invention resides solely in coating unless structural details involved; (B) articles made from a particular material/composition unless structural details involved; (C) laminated structures limited to layer order unless significant structure/arrangement involved; and (D) articles/apparatus/systems distinguished solely by the presence of a particular material (examples given). If a TC determines drawings are necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113, the filing-date issue will be reconsidered and application returned to OPAP for mailing of a Notice of Incomplete Application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Incomplete Application — procedures and applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application lacks required content (e.g., written description, claim, or required drawing), OPAP will mail a "Notice of Incomplete Application" indicating no filing date has been granted and setting a period for applicant response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant options typically include: (A) filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) (with petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(f)) asserting the missing item was submitted or that deposited papers contain an adequate written description, with sufficient evidence (37 CFR 1.181(b)); (B) submitting the omitted material (specification, claim, or drawings) accompanied by an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63/1.64 referring to the submission and accepting the submission date as the filing date; or (C) submitting an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(a). Petitions/filings must comply with the cited CFR provisions. The 2-month period specified is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Omitted Item(s) — when filing date accorded but figures missing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is filed without all drawing figures referred to in the specification but contains something that can be construed as a written description, at least one drawing (if necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113), and at least one claim, OPAP will mail a "Notice of Omitted Item(s)" indicating the papers have been accorded a filing date but are lacking some drawing figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The "Notice of Omitted Item(s)" permits the applicant to: (A) within 2 months file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with evidence establishing prior receipt of the drawing(s) (petition fee refundable if drawing(s) was received); (B) within 2 months submit the omitted drawing(s) in a nonprovisional application with an oath/declaration referencing the drawing(s) plus a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting the later filing date (2-month period not extendable); or (C) accept the application as deposited by failing to file such petitions within 2 months (constructive acceptance), but must then amend the specification to cancel references to omitted drawings, renumber drawing figures via replacement sheets under 37 CFR 1.121(d), and correct references to drawing figures in the specification to correspond to any relabeled figures. Any petitions under 37 CFR 1.53(e) or 1.182 filed after the 2-month period may be dismissed as untimely (37 CFR 1.181(f)). The manual advises applicants to consider filing a new application as a cost-effective alternative to requesting a later filing date by petition, and notes that petitions under 1.182 will not be granted for provisional applications (applicants should file a new provisional instead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict 2-month deadline for petitions regarding omitted items
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.181(f) or related provisions claiming prior receipt or requesting an alternate filing date in response to a Notice of Omitted Item(s) or Notice of Incomplete Application generally must be filed within the 2-month period specified in the notice; the 2-month period is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO may strictly adhere to the 2-month period and dismiss as untimely any petition not filed within the period. Strict adherence is justified because applications forwarded for examination at the end of the 2-month period or because according a later filing date may affect patent term and related rights. Applicants should consider filing a new application if appropriate rather than relying on late petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures when application located in a Technology Center (TC)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application located in a TC was filed without required pages or drawing figures and OPAP has not mailed a notice, the examiner should review the application to determine whether it is entitled to a filing date (i.e., contains something that can be construed as a written description, at least one drawing figure if necessary, and at least one claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entitled to a filing date, the examiner should notify applicant in the next Office action and require the applicant to: (A) accept the application as filed without omitted pages/figures; (B) file omitted pages/figures with an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63/1.64 and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting the submission date as filing date; or (C) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) alleging that the omitted pages/figures were deposited with the application and include supporting evidence. Petitions filed in accord with items (B) or (C) should be filed with the TC which will match the petition to the file and forward to the Office of Petitions with a brief explanation. If the examiner determines the application is NOT entitled to a filing date, the examiner should forward the application to OPAP for mailing of a Notice of Incomplete Application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment requirements when accepting application lacking drawing figures
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant accepts an application as deposited despite omitted drawing figure(s), certain amendments are required to maintain clarity and consistency of the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required submissions include: (1) amendment to the specification canceling all references to the omitted drawing figure(s) including any reference numerals shown only in the omitted figures; (2) replacement sheets of drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) to renumber drawing figures submitted on filing consecutively, if necessary; and (3) a further amendment to the specification correcting references to drawing figures both in the brief and detailed descriptions to correspond with the relabeled drawing figure(s). Such amendments should be submitted in response to the Office action, preferably as a preliminary amendment prior to the first Office action to avoid prosecution delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of numbered-letter drawing figures (e.g., Fig. 1A) and specification errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings are filed with figure labels using number-letter combinations (e.g., Fig. 1A, 1B, 1C) and the specification refers only to the particular number (e.g., Figure 1), OPAP will not mail a Notice of Omitted Item(s) for the missing numbered figure; this is an error in the specification that must be corrected rather than treated as missing figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where drawings include at least one figure labeled with a particular number in combination with a letter, the Office treats a specification reference to the bare number as a specification error needing correction (amendment) rather than a ground to treat the application as filed without all figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition and evidence standards for establishing prior receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions asserting that an omitted item (specification pages, drawing(s), or claims) was in fact deposited with the USPTO must be accompanied by sufficient evidence to establish entitlement to the requested filing date (37 CFR 1.181(b) and (f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence examples include a date-stamped postcard receipt (MPEP § 503) or other documentation establishing prior receipt. Petition fees per 37 CFR 1.17(f) apply; petition fee will be refunded if it is determined the item was in fact received with the application papers deposited on filing. Failure to file within the 2-month period may result in dismissal as untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Attorney content and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The attorney’s or agent’s full mailing address (including ZIP Code) must be given in every power of attorney; telephone and fax numbers should also be included to facilitate prompt communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A power of attorney may be incorporated in the oath or declaration form when given by inventors; otherwise a separate power of attorney (e.g., PTO/SB/81) should be used. See MPEP § 402 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address and daytime telephone requirements and change priority
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an application a correspondence address must be set forth in either an application data sheet (ADS, 37 CFR 1.76) or elsewhere in a clearly identifiable manner in any paper submitted with the application filing; a daytime telephone number is requested pursuant to 37 CFR 1.33(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will direct notices and communications to the person associated with the correspondence address. For electronic filings, an electronic acknowledgment receipt will be sent to the submitter. If more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document, the Office will select one for use and will prefer an address associated with a Customer Number over a typed address. Where multiple documents provide conflicting addresses, priority for which address is used is: (A) Application data sheet (ADS); (B) application transmittal; (C) oath or declaration (unless power of attorney is more current); and (D) power of attorney. The correspondence address may be changed prior to filing of a §1.63 oath/declaration by the party who filed the application or certain named practitioners; after a §1.63 oath/declaration is filed, only the parties set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(b) may change the address (with some exceptions). The Office generally will not engage in double correspondence and will select a single correspondence address for communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP notice/forms practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) no longer uses pre-printed forms and instead uses individualized notices generated by a computer to notify applicants of defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices such as "Notice of Incomplete Application" and "Notice of Omitted Item(s)" are generated individually and will set applicable periods and required procedural steps (including petition fees and evidence requirements). See related MPEP sections for processing and IFW handling.
